title: Tev: Scaling Long-Horizon Agentic Environments with Dense Progress Rewards
why_read: An ambitious attempt to train long-horizon autonomous agents using dense, verifiable progress rewards derived from a hidden task specification, addressing the real sparse-reward bottleneck in agent training.
analysis: Long-horizon agentic tasks, things that take hours or days of autonomous work, are hard to train because success/failure signals only arrive at the very end, giving the model little to learn from along the way. The authors build a dataset of over a thousand tasks with a 'latent world' specification that lets them measure partial progress at every step, then convert that into a dense reward signal for reinforcement learning. The resulting model reportedly matches or beats several named frontier models on agent benchmarks despite being trained on narrower data, which if accurate is a notable result on generalization. The claims about matching named proprietary models should be read with some skepticism since those models and benchmarks move quickly and self-reported comparisons can be cherry-picked.
